newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Lung Kee Metal says all placement shares taken.
newsitem.headline: Lung Kee Metal says all placement shares taken.

text.p: Lung Kee Metal Holdings Ltd (LKMH) said on Monday its entire placement of 40 million shares had been fully subscribed.

This augured well for the remaining 10 million shares being offered to the public in connection with its primary listing on the main board of the Singapore Stock Exchange, Richard Tan of placement agent OUB Bank told a news conference.
The company, a unit of Lung Kee (Bermuda) Holdings Ltd, has offered a total of 50 million shares.
It placed out 40 million shares at US$0.55 each and the rest will be offered to the public at the same price.
"All the 40 million placement shares of 80 percent of issues have already been taken," said Tan, senior vice president of investment banking and corporate finance at OUB Bank.
The offer shares, representing 25 percent of the company's enlarged share capital, have a forecast price earnings ratio of 7.78 times based on the financial year ending on March 31.
This compares with a historical P/E ratio of 8.83, based on the previous financial year.
"Relative to the earning growth potential of the company, the price earning ratios of 8.8 historical and 7.8 prospective, are very undemanding," Tan said.
He said the issue was also competitively priced compared to recent main board IPO issues and against earnings of other companies in the mould base industry.
LKMH aims to raise US$18.1 million, the bulk of which will finance the construction of new plants in China and Malaysia.

The new Guangzhou factory, to be completed early next year, will specialise in making mould bases for the expanding European market, while its Shanghai factory, ready in the second quarter of this year, will cater to rising mainland demand.
In Malaysia, a new factory will start operating mid-1997 to capture regional business.
LKMH chairman Siu Tit Lung said the company had held on to its dominant position due partly to limited competition.

"The mould base industry is capital intensive and requires high technical expertise which are major barriers to entry," he said, adding LKMH had also enjoyed economies of scale and a rise in light manufacturing business in Asia,
LKMH's compounded annual growth rate for the financial years from 1992 to 1996 was 29 percent for turnover, 58 percent for profit before tax and 60 percent for earnings per share.
A mould base is a prefabricated metal mould in which a plastic injection mould is made for the manufacture of a wide range of household and consumer products.
